summary: A 1926 Aermotor steel tower on the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest, NRHP-listed in 1988, once staffed by a ranger who rode out daily from Los Burros Ranger Station.

facts.design: 48-49 ft Aermotor LX-24 steel tower with lookout cab

events.note: Steel tower and cab erected by the Aermotor Windmill Company; USFS periods of significance given as 1925-1949 with 1926 as the key year.
Original ladder to the cab replaced with stairs, sometime in the 1930s (exact year not given).

Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, January 28, 1988, reference 87002453, under the multiple-property submission "National Forest Fire Lookouts in the Southwestern Region." Period of significance given as 1925-1949, with 1926 as the key year. The NPGallery record does not state how many other lookouts or structures the submission covers.
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register, March 4, 2002, nominated by Dave Lorenz, as US 421 / AZ 28.

corrections.proposed: unresolved conflict: NHLR gives 8,467 ft (2,580.7 m); the NRHP/Wikipedia record gives 8,250 ft (~2,514 m)
corrections.evidence: NHLR detail page states elevation 8,467 ft; Wikipedia's summary of the NRHP nomination states 8,250 ft for the same site. No source reconciles the two figures.

corrections.proposed: Aermotor LX-24 steel tower, 48 ft (NHLR) / 49 ft (NRHP via Wikipedia), with lookout cab and ground cabin
corrections.evidence: NHLR detail page gives 48' Aermotor LX-24; the NRHP-derived Wikipedia summary gives 49 ft. The underlying height also isn't settled, so this is offered as a correction candidate rather than a confirmed figure.

sources.title: Lake Mountain Lookout Complex (NRHP #87002453)

notes_for_editor: Good primary-register coverage (NHLR + NRHP nomination metadata + FFLA list), but nothing on named lookouts, specific fires, visitor access, or current staffing/climbability turned up in cache or the three web searches used. The elevation figure conflicts between NHLR (8,467 ft) and the NRHP record (8,250 ft) and should be looked at by someone who can check the actual nomination PDF or a topo map. Height is also given two ways (48 ft vs 49 ft) by the two registers. No cached page existed for this specific lookout outside nhlr/ and ffla/; fflos (abandoned-sites register) has no AZ Lake Mountain entry, consistent with it still standing and in service.
